implementationSummary: Removed the Development services Place tab and its tab-strip link; the map is now a persistent right rail spanning every remaining DS tab (pipeline/inspections/work-orders/code-enforcement/licenses/plan-review/flood-study), matching Overview's existing pattern.

Built the Dock/Expand/Full pill inside web/property-map.js/.html/.css (the map's own iframe), replacing the old external Expand/Full region-bar buttons for the map stage (removed from Overview's rail too, since the in-iframe pill now owns that affordance). The pill posts its mode to the parent shell via postMessage (sc-map-dock-mode) as UI state only, never map data.

THE LAYERS RULE implemented inside the iframe: the categorized 52-layer panel (already existing, category grouping + search) renders full-height only in Full mode; Dock/Expand collapse it to a compact button with the active count that opens the same panel as a sheet on click. No second layer list; still sourced from getAllLayerKeys() via property-map-catalog.mjs, untouched.

Shell listens for the mode message (web/app.js bindMapDockMode()), sets data-map-mode on whichever .shell-regions currently contains the visible map anchor, and calls MountStage.settle() (a plain resize, not the animated modal transitionTo) to reposition the floating iframe onto its new anchor size. New CSS in web/shell.css reflows the lens per mode: Expand shrinks the lens's own primary content to a quiet 250px strip; Full hides it; a shared .mapdock-row wrapper turns the rail's trailing panels from stacked (Dock, display:contents, no override needed) into a side-by-side row (Expand/Full).

New shell-native property-detail panel (zoning, flood zone from the real composePropertyIntelSummary snapshot; buildable area always REFUSED with basis per ruling R-2, independent of fetch outcome) and on-this-parcel records panel (permits+violations+inspections combined, id/subject/status columns only, never free-text description), both fed by the shell calling GET /api/property-map/summary directly -- the SAME route the iframe's own search already calls. No new server route, no map-engine change.

Sliver defect: CONFIRMED as a layout bug, not a component failure. #pm-panel (property-map.html's own search-result aside) carried no `hidden` of its own -- only its child <section>s did -- so it always claimed a fixed flex:0 0 340px inside .pm-layout even with nothing to show. At the ~380px rail width (--sc-rail, web/shell.css) that left #pm-map (the Leaflet canvas) a few pixels: exactly rail-width-minus-340px, reproducible on first paint with zero resize/interaction involved. Rejected mechanism: a Leaflet invalidateSize/stale-container-size failure, ruled out because the effect is a plain CSS flex-basis computation visible before Leaflet ever measures its container, and the observed sliver width matches the arithmetic prediction exactly rather than an arbitrary stale size. Fixed: #pm-panel and this page's own header/search/status chrome hide when embedded (window.self !== window.top); a direct, non-embedded visit to /property-map.html is unchanged.

Bastrop-only refusal and record field allowlist verified by construction: loadPropertyDock() renders the honest not-read/no-match state whenever composePropertyIntelSummary returns non-ok (which it does by design for any cityKey other than its one real pack), and propertyRecordRow() only ever reads .permitNumber/.caseNumber/.type/.status off each record, never spreading or reading a description-shaped field.
